channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Distribuidoras de combustível ameaçam ir à Justiça contra exposição de lucro e podem rejeitar subvenção de R$ 4 bi
item.description: Fuel distributors threaten legal action against the Lula government's requirement to disclose profit margins as a condition for accessing a subsidy of up to R$ 4.33 billion for diesel imports. The companies argue the measure violates commercial confidentiality and may reject the subsidy if the rule is not revised. The dispute highlights tensions over transparency in the energy sector and state intervention in pricing mechanisms.

item.title: 'Bizarro e ilegal', diz Flávio sobre voto de Moraes para condenar Eduardo
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), a pre-candidate for president, criticized Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes' vote condemning his brother, former deputy Eduardo Bolsonaro, in a defamation case brought by federal deputy Tabata Amaral. Flávio called the decision 'bizarre and illegal,' arguing the ruling was politically motivated and unlawful.

item.title: Lula critica Bets e diz querer regulação da redes sociais durante a eleição
item.description: President Lula criticized online sports betting (bets) and called for stricter regulation of social media during elections. He made the remarks alongside Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez during a press conference, following a Quaest poll showing 29% of Brazilians engage in online betting.

item.title: PDT aciona STF para anular eleição de Douglas Ruas na Alerj
item.description: The PDT filed a petition with the STF to annul the election of Douglas Ruas as president of the Alerj, citing irregularities in the vote. The party also requests a new secret-ballot vote and Ruas’s removal from office.

item.title: A enxurrada de startups e PMEs brasileiras na feira de Hannover
item.description: Sebrae will take 190 Brazilian micro, small enterprises and startups to Hannover Messe 2026, the world’s leading industrial technology fair, with Brazil as the official partner country and President Lula confirmed to attend. The mission aims to expand export opportunities and international insertion for small businesses, highlighting companies such as Easypro Tech, which develops industrial time-analysis software, and Biosolvit, focused on sustainability and circular economy solutions.

item.title: Gonet é contra livrar Roberto Jefferson de multa no STF
item.description: Attorney General Paulo Gonet advised Minister Alexandre de Moraes that Roberto Jefferson should not be exempt from the STF-imposed fine, but that the payment should be made in equal monthly installments. Gonet argued that the defense failed to satisfactorily prove Jefferson’s inability to pay, given the updated fine of R$ 972,600. Moraes’ order for Jefferson to pay within ten days stands, with judicial enforcement possible if not complied with voluntarily.

item.title: ‘Sua dedicação elevou o nome do País’, diz Lula; veja reações à morte de Oscar Schmidt
item.description: President Lula mourned the death of Oscar Schmidt, a Brazilian basketball legend, praising his dedication, talent, and love for the national team, and highlighting the 1987 Pan-American Games victory over the U.S. as a symbolic moment. Other authorities, including Vice President Alckmin, Senate President Alcolumbre, and Chamber President Motta, paid tribute, emphasizing his sporting legacy and global impact.

item.title: Oscar Schmidt tentou carreira política e sonhou com a Presidência
item.description: Oscar Schmidt, former basketball star, entered Brazilian politics in the 1990s, running for the São Paulo Senate in 1990 and losing to Eduardo Suplicy in 1998. In a 2025 interview, he revealed his Senate bid was part of a larger plan to run for President of Brazil after spending 13 years in Europe. Prior to the Senate race, he served as municipal secretary of Sports, Leisure, and Recreation in São Paulo (1997–1998) under Mayor Celso Pitta.

item.title: Governo federal decreta luto de 3 dias pela morte de Oscar Schmidt
item.description: Acting President Geraldo Alckmin declared three days of official mourning for the death of Oscar Schmidt, Brazilian basketball legend, at age 68. Lula also expressed sorrow, praising Schmidt as a model of determination, talent, and love for the national team.

item.title: Lula lamenta morte de Oscar Schmidt e celebra legado no basquete
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva mourned the death of Oscar Schmidt, a basketball legend, praising his legacy as a symbol of talent, perseverance, and love for the Brazilian national team. Lula said Schmidt united the country around basketball courts and inspired generations of athletes. The 68-year-old former player died after being hospitalized for sudden illness, with a known history of a brain tumor diagnosed in 2011.

item.title: RJ: Douglas Ruas e governador interino se reúnem após eleição da Alerj
item.description: Douglas Ruas (PL), newly elected president of the Rio de Janeiro State Legislature (Alerj), met with interim governor Ricardo Couto to affirm his commitment to institutional normalcy. He aims to dialogue with the Supreme Federal Court (STF) regarding the state’s succession line, as Couto’s continued tenure blocks Ruas from assuming the interim governorship. Ruas criticized ongoing institutional interinities and said Alerj’s legal office will notify the STF of his election to prompt a reevaluation of the succession.

item.title: Plínio diz que governo trava PEC da autonomia do BC e apresenta novo parecer
item.description: Senator Plínio Valério (PSDB-AM), rapporteur of the Central Bank autonomy PEC, presented a new opinion stating that the federal government does not intend to advance the proposal in 2026 due to the electoral context. The revised text consolidates adjustments made over a year, including reclassifying the BC as a 'public entity of special nature' to eliminate private law ambiguities, increasing articles from 8 to 10, strengthening governance, granting the BC authority over its own remuneration, pension management, and budget control — subject to CMN and Senate approval — and authorizing interventions during financial crises.

item.title: Políticos lamentam morte de Oscar Schmidt
item.description: Politicians mourned the death of Oscar Schmidt, former basketball player known as 'Holy Hand,' emphasizing his significance to Brazilian and global sports. Vice President Geraldo Alckmin, Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), and other officials praised his career, noting his brain cancer diagnosis in 2011 and nearly three decades of play for clubs including Palmeiras, Sírio, Corinthians, Flamengo, and European teams.

item.title: Acórdão do TSE não define modelo de eleição-tampão no RJ
item.description: The TSE ruling that made former Rio de Janeiro governor Cláudio Castro (PL) ineligible did not specify whether the interim election for the state mandate will be direct or indirect. The decision on the model is pending analysis at the STF. The case concerns the state succession following Castro’s ineligibility.

item.title: Lula/X: Oscar Schmidt é exemplo de obstinaçăo, talento e de amor ŕ camisa da seleçăo
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva paid tribute to the late basketball legend Oscar Schmidt, who died at 68, calling him an example of persistence, talent, and love for the national team. The message was posted on X (formerly Twitter) on Friday, the 17th.

item.title: Flávio aparece em vídeo ao lado de assessor de Marçal que socou marqueteiro do PL
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) appeared in a video alongside Nahuel Medina, Pablo Marçal's aide who assaulted PL's campaign strategist Duda Lima during a 2024 electoral debate. Recorded in Alphaville, Flávio praised Medina and offered entrepreneurial advice, while Medina admitted his reaction was impulsive and intends to personally apologize to Lima.

item.title: Pesquisa Quaest indica o principal problema para Lula e os motivos para avanço de Flávio
item.description: The Quaest poll shows a technical tie between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro in the runoff, with Lula leading 37% to 32% in the first round. The government’s 52% disapproval and negative economic perception — despite positive macro indicators — are Lula’s main hurdles, as voters don’t feel financial improvement. Flávio Bolsonaro gains by capitalizing on government weariness and the perception that social programs are no longer electoral differentiators.

item.title: Presidente Lula e Ministério do Esporte homenageiam Oscar Schmidt: 'Maior ídolo da história do basquete brasileiro'
item.description: President Lula and the Ministry of Sports paid tribute to Oscar Schmidt, the legendary Brazilian basketball player who passed away at 68, honoring him as the greatest idol in Brazilian basketball history and one of the sport’s all-time top scorers. Lula highlighted Schmidt’s perseverance, talent, and dedication to the national team, while the Ministry emphasized his remarkable career totals — 49.737 points (second-highest in global basketball history) and 7.693 for Brazil — along with his gold medal at the 1987 Pan American Games and appearances in five Olympic Games from 1980 to 1996.

item.title: Malufista, Oscar Schmidt concorreu ao Senado e sonhou com a Presidência
item.description: Oscar Schmidt, Brazilian basketball idol, entered politics in 1998 as a Senate candidate for the PPB (now PP), backed by Paulo Maluf and strategist Duda Mendonça. Although he came close to winning, he lost to Eduardo Suplicy (PT). Years later, he revealed his ambition was to use the Senate as a stepping stone to the presidency.

item.title: PDT nacional aciona STF para anular eleição na Alerj que elegeu Douglas Ruas como presidente
item.description: The national PDT has filed a petition with the STF to annul the election that chose Douglas Ruas (PL) as president of the Alerj, citing interference from drug trafficking and militias and demanding a secret ballot. The party seeks Ruas’s immediate removal until a new vote is held under secret ballot rules, arguing that the STF has already signaled favor toward secret voting in indirect or sensitive elections.

item.title: Boulos diz que relator de PL dos apps cedeu a lobby de plataformas
item.description: Guilherme Boulos accused rapporteur Augusto Coutinho of yielding to platform lobbying from iFood and Uber by rolling back worker protections in a revised version of the PLP 152/2025 bill. The Lula government opposes the R$ 8.50 per ride floor, advocating for R$ 10 plus a per-kilometer addition, aligned with worker demands. Boulos denied a rift between the government and app workers, stating both oppose the current bill and that the government has expanded dialogue with unions, local associations, and worker movements.

item.title: Bolsonaro tem “boa evolução do quadro pulmonar e digestivo”, diz médico
item.description: Former President Jair Bolsonaro has shown good progress in his pulmonary and digestive condition, according to a medical report sent to the STF, with improvement in symptoms such as fatigue, reflux, and shortness of breath, along with increased physical stamina.

item.title: Ministro defende projeto do governo pelo fim da escala 6x1 e diz que reduzir para 36 horas é 'irresponsabilidade'
item.description: Labor Minister Luiz Marinho defended the government's bill to end the 6x1 work scale, stating that an immediate reduction to 36 weekly hours would be irresponsible. He argued that Brazil's economy can sustain a more gradual reduction to 40 hours per week, as proposed by the executive.

item.title: O que pensam os eleitores sobre a suposta ‘moderação’ de Flávio Bolsonaro, segundo a Quaest
item.description: A Quaest poll reveals 45% of voters do not see Flávio Bolsonaro as more moderate than his family, compared to 39% who do. For Lula, there is a technical tie: 42% view him as more moderate than the PT, while 42% hold the opposite view. Ronaldo Caiado is seen as the most moderate candidate by only 20%, with 39% disagreeing and 41% undecided.

item.title: ‘Estamos imersos em uma crise’, diz o presidente do STF
item.description: Supreme Federal Court President Minister Edson Fachin warned that the Brazilian Judiciary is immersed in an institutional crisis marked by distrust and polarization, noting that judicial actions perceived as political erode public trust. He emphasized the need to recognize and confront this crisis with new approaches, avoiding repeated ineffective solutions. The statement comes amid internal tensions in the Court, including attempts to indict ministers by the Organized Crime CPI and investigations linked to Banco Master.

item.title: “Vamos ter mais um ministro censurador no STF?”, questiona Deltan
item.description: Deltan Dallagnol criticized the extrajudicial notice issued by the AGU, at the request of Deputy Erika Hilton, against journalists and influencers over publications about the so-called 'Misogyny Bill,' calling it persecution and censorship. He questioned whether AGU Chief Minister Jorge Messias is becoming a 'censoring minister' at the STF. The article was published by O Antagonista.

item.title: Lula lidera, mas PT vê eleição aberta e prepara batalha pelo centro
item.description: Lula leads in internal PT polls for 2026, but the party views the election as open and is preparing a battle for the center-right vote, particularly in the three states with the most voters. PT Secretary-General Henrique Fontana says the race will be decided by 2% or 3% of centrist voters and compares the importance of the 2026 election to that of 2022.

item.title: Clica e Confirma: TSE elege ministro Nunes Marques para a Presidência do Tribunal
item.description: Minister Nunes Marques was elected president of the Superior Electoral Court (TSE) and Minister André Mendonça as vice-president, assuming leadership of Brazil’s Electoral Justice for the 2026 elections. The election was conducted via electronic voting among TSE ministers. The program also highlights Indigenous Peoples’ Day, the TSE’s efforts to ensure indigenous political inclusion, and a visit by a delegation from Mozambique’s Constitutional Council.

item.title: Papo Antagonista: Lula volta a defender regulação digital durante visita à Espanha
item.description: During a visit to Spain, President Lula advocated for stronger regulation of social media in Brazil to prevent 'foreign interference in election years,' reinforcing his stance on digital sovereignty. He also referenced the Genial/Quaest poll showing that 29% of Brazilians regularly engage in online sports betting, raising concerns about its social impact. The Papo Antagonista segment analyzed both issues in a critical assessment of the current political and social landscape.

item.title: Não aceitarei “inversão de papéis”, diz Gaspar sobre Lindbergh e Soraya
item.description: Deputy Alfredo Gaspar (PL-AL) rejected accusations of slander, defamation, and injuria from Lindbergh Farias (PT-RJ) and Soraya Thronicke (PSB-MS), claiming he is the victim of an unproven serious accusation. He denied committing rape of a vulnerable person and said the charges aim to discredit his INSS CPMI report. Gaspar said he will respond to the STF with concrete evidence and hopes the Ethics Committees of the Chamber and Senate will review his requests for the impeachment of his accusers.

item.title: Fachin diz que Judiciário vive crise e defende autocontenção do STF
item.description: STF President Edson Fachin stated that the Judiciary is facing a crisis and requires self-restraint and critical reflection on its limits. He emphasized that expansions of power must be accompanied by limits to avoid inadequate solutions for new problems. Fachin also highlighted the importance of using legal mechanisms, such as appeals, rather than attacking institutionality during disagreements.

item.title: Assessor de Marçal que agrediu marqueteiro grava vídeo com Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Nahuel Medina, an aide to Pablo Marçal who assaulted marketer Duda Lima in 2024, posted a video with Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), a presidential pre-candidate. Lima, a marketer for the Liberal Party, has seen his circle express outrage over the association, according to O Antagonista. The incident rekindles tensions between Marçal’s allies and Bolsonaro-aligned figures.

item.title: Bolsa Família volta a crescer e encosta nos 19 milhões de pagamentos
item.description: The Bolsa Família program reached 19 million payments in April 2026, recovering from a 2025 decline, though the average benefit per family dropped to R$678.22. Despite the rise in beneficiaries, total spending remained stable at R$12.8 billion due to the lower average payment. Experts suggest possible fraud, such as spouse omission and informal work to retain benefits, with 895,000 families receiving more in aid than from formal employment.

item.title: Girão defende reação do Senado contra atos do STF
item.description: Senator Eduardo Girão (Novo-CE) defended in the Senate plenary the need for greater initiative by the House regarding STF decisions, stating the Senate faces difficulties exercising its prerogatives and denouncing legal insecurity in the country. He criticized STF ministers, especially Gilmar Mendes, for requesting an investigation against Senator Alessandro Vieira (MDB-SE) following his report in the Organized Crime CPI, alleging abuse of authority, and called the episode an attack on parliamentary immunity. Girão stated the Senate must admit the first impeachment process against an STF minister to prevent the 'togato dictatorship' and restore balance among the Powers.

item.title: Quase senador e sonho de Presidência: a decepção de Oscar Schmidt com a política
item.description: Oscar Schmidt, Brazilian basketball legend known as 'Mão Santa', died at age 66 on Friday. Beyond his sports career, he had a brief political stint in the 1990s, serving as municipal secretary of Sports in São Paulo and running for Senate under the PPB in 1998, where he placed second with over 5.7 million votes, losing to Eduardo Suplicy. Despite aspiring to the presidency, Schmidt became disillusioned with politics and withdrew from public life, stating in a 2024 interview that he was 'grateful to God' for not being elected.

item.title: Por Dentro das Eleições: Brasil utiliza sistemas eleitorais majoritário e proporcional
item.description: Brazil uses a mixed electoral system for the 2026 elections: majoritarian for executive offices (president, governor, mayor) and the Senate, and proportional for federal, state, district deputies and city council members. In majoritarian races, the candidate with the most votes wins (simple or absolute majority). In proportional representation, seats are allocated based on the total votes received by each party or federation, favoring the highest-voted candidates within each list.

item.title: Médicos indicam a possibilidade de mais uma cirurgia em Bolsonaro
item.description: Jair Bolsonaro's medical team told Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes that the former president is fit for surgery on his right shoulder, citing persistent pain during movement. Bolsonaro is currently under temporary house arrest following hospitalization for bilateral bacterial pneumonia due to bronchoaspiration, which had put his life at risk. The medical report was submitted to the STF as part of the review process for the precautionary measure, set to be reassessed in June.

item.title: STF tem maioria para manter decisão do TSE que cassou Rodrigo Bacellar
item.description: The First Chamber of the STF formed a majority to deny the appeal and uphold the removal and ineligibility of former Alerj president Rodrigo Bacellar, confirming the TSE's decision. Rapporteur Cristiano Zanin was joined by Alexandre de Moraes and Flávio Dino, with only Minister Cármen Lúcia's vote pending until April 28. The ruling deemed the appeal premature, as the TSE's full court may still review the decision.

item.title: Flávio diz que Moraes vai usar o STF para desequilibrar as eleições
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) accused Minister Alexandre de Moraes of using his position at the STF to interfere in the 2026 elections, claiming the inquiry opened against him for slander against Lula is part of a strategy to unbalance the race and silence right-wing opponents. He stated that the 'fake news' inquiry, opened seven years ago, will be repeatedly used during the campaign to restrict his freedom of speech. Senate President Rodrigo Pacheco (misidentified as 'Alcolumbre' in the text) offered legal support to senators to defend the legitimacy of the vote and parliamentary prerogatives.

item.title: Como a capital de JK se tornou centro da tecnologia eleitoral e o futuro da democracia
item.description: Brasília, Brazil's capital founded 66 years ago, has become the nation's electoral technology hub by hosting the Superior Electoral Court (TSE), which designed, tested, and validated the electronic voting system now recognized globally for its transparency and auditability. As a symbol of Brazilian modernity since the Juscelino Kubitschek era, the city now serves as the 'central nervous system' of democracy, where the voting machines' source code is opened for inspection by political parties, universities, and the Armed Forces before each election, reinforcing public trust in the electoral process.

item.title: Uma ‘batalha antiga’ entre Lula e Flávio volta com força, e deve mexer com as pesquisas
item.description: The 2026 Brazilian presidential election is shaped by a renewed 'old battle' between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro over the religious vote, particularly among Catholics and evangelicals. Flávio Bolsonaro is actively courting evangelicals through frequent church visits and biblical references, while Lula faces declining support in this group, with over 60% rejection among evangelicals driven by influential right-wing religious leaders like Silas Malafaia. Although Lula still holds a significant lead among Catholics, recent surveys show erosion in this traditionally PT-aligned base, prompting analysts to urge the government to defend its Catholic voter bloc amid a highly polarized and tight race.

item.title: Hugo Motta diz que espera que veto de Lula ao PL da Dosimetria seja derrubado
item.description: Speaker of the Chamber of Deputies Hugo Motta expressed hope that Congress will overturn President Lula's veto on the Dosimetry Bill, which would reduce sentences for crimes related to January 8, including Jair Bolsonaro's sentence from 27 years and 3 months to 20 years. He argues the measure could ease tensions between branches by correcting what legislators see as excessive penalties. Senate President Davi Alcolumbre has scheduled the veto vote for the 30th.

item.title: Acórdão do julgamento de Castro no TSE é concluído e não estipula se eleição para mandato-tampão no Rio será direta ou indireta
item.description: The TSE's ruling that made Claudio Castro ineligible has been finalized but does not specify whether the interim mandate election in Rio will be direct or indirect, pending STF decision. Castro resigned before the ruling, which opponents claim was a maneuver to avoid disqualification. The STF awaits the acórdão's publication to resume judging the election format.

item.title: Oscar Schmidt queria ser presidente, tentou vaga no Senado e foi Secretário de Esporte
item.description: Oscar Schmidt, Brazil's basketball idol, died at 68 in São Paulo. Before his death, he ventured into politics in the 1990s, serving as Municipal Secretary of Sports in São Paulo (1997-1998) and running for Senate in 1998, where he lost to Eduardo Suplicy. He stated his Senate bid was part of a larger ambition to become President of Brazil.

item.title: Kassio vota por derrubar lei da Bahia que pune desinformação sobre pandemias
item.description: Minister Kassio Nunes Marques voted to strike down a Bahia law that penalizes the spread of false information about pandemics, epidemics, or endemics with fines up to R$20,000. He argued the law overstepped state authority by encroaching on federal powers, particularly by sanctioning telecom concessionaires, and violated freedom of expression. The judgment is taking place in the STF’s virtual plenary until April 28, with opposing views from the AGU and PGR.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro supera Lula em engajamento no Instagram, aponta levantamento
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro surpassed Lula in Instagram engagement in March, recording 24.1 million interactions — 2.56 times more than the president. He posted more (128 vs 105) and achieved a 2.1x higher average engagement per post (188,413 vs 89,607), with nine of the top ten most engaging posts belonging to him. Despite this, polls show Lula leading in the first round.

item.title: Deltan doa sobra de R$ 730 mil arrecadado em vaquinha para indenizar Lula
item.description: Former prosecutor Deltan Dallagnol donated R$ 730,000 to Erastinho Hospital in Curitiba, representing the surplus from donations collected to pay a R$ 146,000 moral damages indemnity to President Lula, following a court decision upheld by the STF. He noted the funds came from over 12,000 Pix donations ranging from R$ 5 to R$ 1,000, with an additional R$ 5,000 from his own pocket. Dallagnol praised donors as 'true heroes' and said directing the surplus to the hospital was a way to 'defeat evil with good'.

item.title: Juiz vê ‘perseguição política’ contra Erika Hilton e rejeita ação de ONG
item.description: Judge Giordano Resende Costa of the 4th Civil Court of Brasília dismissed a public civil action filed by NGO Matria against federal deputy Erika Hilton (PSOL-SP), citing a 'clear bias of political persecution' and protecting her under parliamentary immunity. The suit sought a retraction over Hilton’s social media post criticizing 'transphobes and imbeCIS', a play on 'cis' referring to cisgender individuals opposing trans women’s recognition. The judge stated the NGO aims to silence a lawmaker through judicial means, transforming legitimate ideological disagreement into a punitive R$500,000 claim.

item.title: Ricardo Couto deve ficar no governo até o fim do ano
item.description: The STF has maintained an injunction freezing the succession of the Rio de Janeiro state government, keeping Judge Ricardo Couto in office until the end of the year to avoid holding two costly elections. The decision awaits a plenary ruling and the TSE’s final decision on Claudio Castro’s cassation. Eduardo Paes’ group lost the legislative election, reflecting Castro’s control over the state apparatus.

item.title: Motta diz que apoia derrubada de vetos de Lula ao projeto da redução de penas do 8/1
item.description: Chamber of Deputies President Hugo Motta (Republicanos-PB) expressed support for overturning President Lula's veto on a bill reducing sentences for those convicted of coup d'état. The measure could benefit former President Jair Bolsonaro (PL), currently under house arrest. The statement was made on Friday, April 17, 2026.
